bindings.stack_element_alloc.allocator_owns_eleme: the ownership fact corresponding to `new_Element(*n, parser)`; `new_Element` expands to placement new on `allocator.Allocate(sizeof(Element))`, so the constructed `element` is parser `StackAllocator` storage rather than ordinary `new` storage
bindings.eof_cleanup_guard.plain_delete_enabled: the branch truth corresponding to whether the non-top-level EOF cleanup executes `delete element;`; in the vulnerable original this is the unconditional fallthrough to `delete element;` once `n == nullptr` and `!topLevel` are reached
bindings.eof_cleanup_guard.plain_delete_allowed: the ownership conjunct corresponding to whether `element` names ordinary heap storage eligible for plain `delete`; on this tracked path it is false because `element` was constructed by `new_Element(*n, parser)` / `allocator.Allocate(sizeof(Element))`

note: The `*.true_literal` operand is a compile-time literal field emitted at the event and is intentionally omitted from `bindings`.
